name: xfs_rmap_convert
prose: Converts the written/unwritten state of the rmap range [bno, bno+len) for the inode owner decoded from oinfo, on the rmap btree cursor cur. It decodes owner and offset with xfs_owner_info_unpack (debug ASSERT that the owner is an inode owner and that no attr-fork or bmbt-block flag is set), then does xfs_rmap_lookup_le for the record PREV at bno with flag oldext (XFS_RMAP_UNWRITTEN if unwritten, else 0); coverage of the range by PREV is only checked by debug ASSERTs on PREV.rm_offset <= offset, PREV end >= offset+len and PREV flag == oldext. It then sets LEFT_FILLING / RIGHT_FILLING from whether PREV starts at offset / ends at offset+len, steps the cursor to the left neighbour (LEFT, tested for contiguity with the new flags newext = ~oldext & XFS_RMAP_UNWRITTEN) and to the right neighbour (RIGHT), and clears RIGHT_CONTIG if the combined left+len+right length would exceed XFS_RMAP_LEN_MAX in the fully merged case. A switch on the four FILLING/CONTIG bits then updates, deletes (xfs_btree_delete) and inserts (xfs_btree_insert) records to merge with left and/or right or to split PREV into up to three records; combinations not handled (such as a CONTIG bit without its FILLING bit) hit ASSERT(0) and, if asserts are compiled out, leave the btree unchanged and fall through to a return of 0. Returns 0 on completion, or a negative errno from a failed btree helper, or -EFSCORRUPTED (after xfs_btree_mark_sick) when a lookup, get_rec, increment, decrement, delete or insert reports an unexpected count (i != 1, or i != 0 for the lookup_eq in the split cases), when LEFT ends after bno, or when RIGHT starts before bno+len. All error exits go through done, which only adds a trace, so the btree may be left partially modified after a mid-sequence error. No locks or references are taken or released here.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function xfs_rmap_convert at xfs_rmap.c:1248-1738 read in full. Reviewer claim (no delete, overlap only asserted) is WRONG: xfs_btree_delete is called at lines 1426/1445/1476/1515 and overlap of LEFT/RIGHT returns -EFSCORRUPTED at 1330 and 1368-1371. Prose rewritten to list the default-case ASSERT(0) path and the LEN_MAX clamp.

name: xfs_rmap_convert_shared
prose: Same job as xfs_rmap_convert but for the reflink (shared) variant: converts the written/unwritten state of [bno, bno+len) for the inode owner decoded from oinfo (debug ASSERT that it is an inode owner without attr-fork or bmbt-block flags). It finds PREV with xfs_rmap_lookup_le_range (i != 1 gives -EFSCORRUPTED after xfs_btree_mark_sick), sets LEFT_FILLING / RIGHT_FILLING, finds the left neighbour with xfs_rmap_find_left_neighbor (LEFT ending after bno gives -EFSCORRUPTED) and the right neighbour with xfs_rmap_lookup_eq at bno+len (RIGHT starting before bno+len gives -EFSCORRUPTED), sets the CONTIG bits using xfs_rmap_is_mergeable against newext = ~oldext & XFS_RMAP_UNWRITTEN, and clamps RIGHT_CONTIG if the fully merged length would exceed XFS_RMAP_LEN_MAX. A switch on the FILLING/CONTIG bits then rewrites records with xfs_rmap_delete, xfs_rmap_insert, xfs_rmap_lookup_eq (re-positioning the cursor; i != 1 gives -EFSCORRUPTED) and xfs_rmap_update to merge or split PREV; unhandled bit combinations hit ASSERT(0) and, with asserts compiled out, change nothing. Returns 0 on completion or the negative errno from the failing helper / -EFSCORRUPTED; all errors exit via done, which only traces, so the btree may be partly modified. No locks or references are taken or released here.
note: Slice only held the tail of this function (2071-2161) plus xfs_rmap_unmap_shared; earlier rounds called it xfs_rmap_convert but the real function is xfs_rmap_convert_shared (xfs_rmap.c:1746-2161, read in full). Reviewer claim (omits a state parameter) is WRONG: there is no state parameter; state is a local; signature is (cur, bno, len, unwritten, oinfo).

name: xfs_rmap_intent_init_cache
prose: Creates a kmem cache named "xfs_rmap_intent" for objects of size sizeof(struct xfs_rmap_intent) (alignment 0, no flags, no constructor) and stores the pointer in the global xfs_rmap_intent_cache (xfs_rmap.c:3130-3132). Returns 0 if the stored pointer is non-NULL and -ENOMEM if kmem_cache_create returned NULL, in which case the global is NULL as stored. It does not check whether the global was already set, so a previous cache pointer would be overwritten. Takes no locks. Marked __init.
note: Prose rewritten to match code at 3127-3135; contract dropped because the function writes a global (rule 4); the mechanical complaint was the old contract omitting -ENOMEM.

name: xrep_bmap_cow
prose: Repairs the COW fork of the inode sc->ip (cow_repair.c:704-810). Early returns before anything is allocated: -EOPNOTSUPP if the filesystem lacks the rmapbt or reflink feature; 0 if the inode has no COW fork; -EOPNOTSUPP if the inode has big realtime allocation, or is a metadir inode that is realtime; and if the COW fork format is not XFS_DINODE_FMT_EXTENTS it is reset to extents format with if_nextents = 0 and 0 is returned. Otherwise it allocates a struct xrep_cow with kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure, nothing else done), joins sc->ip to sc->tp with xfs_trans_ijoin, and initialises the bad-file-offset bitmap and the old-cow-fork block bitmap (realtime or fs-block flavour depending on the inode). It then walks every COW-fork extent, skipping delalloc (null startblock) and written extents, and calls xrep_cow_find_bad_rt or xrep_cow_find_bad on the rest; walks the bad file offsets with xoff_bitmap_walk calling xrep_cow_replace; and reaps the old COW blocks with xrep_reap_rtblocks or xrep_reap_fsblocks using XFS_RMAP_OINFO_COW. Any error from xchk_should_terminate, find_bad, the walk or the reap jumps to out_bitmap, which destroys the bitmaps, frees xc and returns that error; the same label is also reached on success, returning 0 if nothing failed. Replacements already made are not undone on a later error.
note: Slice cut the head (it started inside the function body, no name); real function xrep_bmap_cow at cow_repair.c:704-810. Earlier prose said only 'on error jumps to out_bitmap' and missed the five early returns and the extents-format reset; the earlier 'dropped' status was only due to no name in the slice.

name: xrep_dirtree_keep_one_good_path
prose: Walks every path in dl (xchk_dirtree_for_each_path) and acts on path->outcome: for XCHK_DIRPATH_CORRUPT or XCHK_DIRPATH_LOOP it decrements oc->suspect, increments oc->bad and sets the outcome to XCHK_DIRPATH_DELETE through xrep_dirpath_set_outcome; for the first XCHK_DIRPATH_OK path it calls xrep_dirpath_retain_parent and leaves the outcome OK; for each later OK path it decrements oc->good, increments oc->bad and sets the outcome to DELETE; paths with any other outcome are left unchanged. xrep_dirpath_retain_parent loads the path first step with xfarray_load and, only if that succeeds, stores the step parent inode number in dl->parent_ino; a load error is silently ignored and dl->parent_ino is unchanged. The function returns nothing and reports no error. It ends with debug-only ASSERTs that oc->suspect == 0 and oc->good < 2; these are not checked when ASSERT is compiled out, and the counts depend on the caller having filled oc via xchk_dirtree_evaluate. Its caller xrep_dirtree_decide_fate only calls it when oc->good > 0.
note: Checked dirtree_repair.c:142-175 and retain_parent 97-110. Reviewer claim that no assertion fires when there is no OK path is RIGHT but is not a prose error: the caller only invokes this when oc->good > 0 (line 245) and the prose states there need not be an OK path; wording now says asserts are debug-only. Round-2 note about silent xfarray_load failure is RIGHT and kept.

name: xrep_symlink_rebuild
prose: Rebuilds the repaired symlink from the salvaged target string in sc->buf (symlink_repair.c:387-482). It computes target_len = strlen(sc->buf); if it is 0 or greater than XFS_SYMLINK_MAXLEN it returns -EFSCORRUPTED before touching any lock. Otherwise it drops sc->ip XFS_ILOCK_EXCL (xchk_iunlock), takes the temp file ILOCK (xrep_tempfile_ilock), joins the temp inode to sc->tp, reserves quota blocks for the target (xfs_trans_reserve_quota_nblks with force=true), discards the temp inode data fork and sets it to extents format with zero bytes, and writes the target into the temp inode with xfs_symlink_write_target; an error from the quota reservation or the write is returned at that point with the repaired inode unlocked, the temp inode locked and joined to sc->tp, and nothing committed. It then calls xrep_trans_commit (which clears sc->tp whether or not the commit succeeded, so a nonzero return does not show the changes were committed); a commit error is returned. Next it returns the error if xchk_should_terminate reports one (temp ILOCK still held), otherwise releases the temp file lock with xrep_tempfile_iunlock, allocates the exchange transaction with xrep_tempexch_trans_alloc (data fork), runs xrep_symlink_swap, and finally returns the result of xrep_symlink_reset_fork, which reaps the temp fork if it has extents and writes the one-byte target "?" into the temp inode. The function returns 0 only when all of these steps return 0; at that point the new transaction in sc->tp has not been committed (xrep_symlink commits it afterwards). The lock state after failures of xrep_tempexch_trans_alloc, xrep_symlink_swap and xrep_symlink_reset_fork is determined by those callees and is not established here.
note: Read symlink_repair.c:340-482 and xrep_trans_commit (repair.h:34-41). Reviewer round-15 claim (a failed xrep_trans_commit typically means not committed) is RIGHT: sc->tp is cleared regardless and a nonzero return does not prove commit, so wording changed. Round-2 claim (xchk_should_terminate failure returns before temp ILOCK is released) is RIGHT (line 453-454) and was already in the old prose. Original claim (early errors have no earlier committed transaction) is RIGHT and already in old prose.

name: xfs_file_write_checks
prose: Pre-write validation for an XFS buffered or direct write; iocb->ki_filp->f_mapping->host is the inode, *iolock records the IOLOCK mode the caller holds (shared or exclusive), and ac is an optional zone allocation context passed to zeroing. It calls generic_write_checks; if that returns <= 0 (0 for an empty write, negative on error) that value is returned at once with the lock unchanged. If IOCB_NOWAIT is set it calls break_layout (converting -EWOULDBLOCK to -EAGAIN) else xfs_break_layouts, which may change *iolock; a nonzero result is returned with the lock still held as recorded in *iolock. If *iolock is XFS_IOLOCK_SHARED and the inode is not IS_NOSEC, it drops the shared lock, sets *iolock to XFS_IOLOCK_EXCL, reacquires via xfs_ilock_iocb (try-lock with -EAGAIN under IOCB_NOWAIT, else blocking); if that returns an error the function sets *iolock to 0 and returns the error with the IOLOCK not held; otherwise it restarts from generic_write_checks. If ki_pos is beyond i_size_read, it calls xfs_file_write_zero_eof: that returns 0 if ki_pos <= isize under i_flags_lock, -EAGAIN under IOCB_NOWAIT, 1 the first time a drain is needed (after possibly upgrading a shared IOLOCK to exclusive, re-expanding the iterator, and waiting with inode_dio_wait; this makes write_checks restart once with drained_dio set), or else zeroes the range with xfs_zero_range under XFS_MMAPLOCK_EXCL and returns its result. A nonzero error other than 1 is returned with *iolock as it then stands (held). If all checks pass it returns kiocb_modified(iocb), which is 0 or a negative error. A positive value is never returned.
note: Read xfs_file.c:353-489 and xfs_ilock_iocb 183-197. Reviewer claim 1 (errors from generic_write_checks, break_layouts, zero_eof, kiocb_modified leave *iolock held) is RIGHT; old prose wrongly implied only the upgrade failure case but also said xfs_file_write_zero_eof 'returns 1 which is never returned', which is WRONG (it returns 1 at xfs_file.c:407). Claim 2 (zero-count generic_write_checks returns 0 early) is RIGHT; old prose did say that, kept. Prose rewritten.

name: xfs_getfsmap_rtdev_rmapbt
prose: Reports fsmap records for the realtime device from the rtgroup rmap btrees, for the key range keys[0]..keys[1] in transaction tp, filling the getfsmap context info (xfs_fsmap.c:874-1040). If keys[0].fmr_physical is at or beyond XFS_FSB_TO_BB(sb_rtstart + sb_rblocks) it returns 0 immediately, before setting info->missing_owner and without taking any lock. On a zoned filesystem with the low key below rtstart_daddr it advances key0 past the previous record, may report an XFS_RMAP_OWN_FS record of length rtstart_daddr through xfs_getfsmap_helper (returning any nonzero error from it), and clears key0 owner, offset and length. It then sets info->missing_owner to XFS_FMR_OWN_FREE and converts the low key via xfs_fsmap_owner_to_rmap (error returned, nothing held); if the unshareable-owner adjustment pushes start_rtb to a daddr at or beyond eofs it returns 0. It then loops over rtgroups with xfs_rtgroup_next_range from start_rg to end_rg (each call returns a referenced rtgroup): sets info->group, for the last group builds the high key from keys[1] (break with the error if owner_to_rmap fails), releases the previous group's XFS_RTGLOCK_RMAP | XFS_RTGLOCK_REFCOUNT lock and deletes its cursor, calls xfs_getfsmap_rtdev_rmapbt_query (takes that lock, creates the cursor, runs xfs_rmap_query_range; error breaks), clears info->low after the first group, and for the last group sets info->last and reports the trailing gap via xfs_getfsmap_rtdev_rmapbt_helper (error breaks), then sets info->group to NULL. After the loop any remaining cursor is unlocked and deleted (XFS_BTREE_ERROR if error < 0), and if the loop was exited by break the rtgroup reference is released with xfs_rtgroup_rele and info->group is set to NULL. It returns 0 if the loop finished without error, otherwise the first nonzero error from owner_to_rmap, the query or the gap helper.
note: Read xfs_fsmap.c:874-1040. Round-1 and round-2 reviewer claims (early eofs return omitted / skips missing_owner) are RIGHT and are stated explicitly. Round-15 claim (info->group left set on error-break paths) is WRONG: xfs_fsmap.c:1035-1038 sets info->group = NULL when rtg is non-NULL after a break. Also says nonzero rather than negative since helper return values are not shown to be only negative.

name: xfs_find_handle
prose: Builds a file handle (or fs handle) and copies it to user space (xfs_handle.c:81-140). For cmd == XFS_IOC_FD_TO_HANDLE it uses the open file hreq->fd, returning -EBADF if there is no such file, and takes its own path reference with path_get on the file path; otherwise it resolves hreq->path with user_path_at (AT_FDCWD, no flags) and returns that function's error if it fails, holding no reference in either early-return case. With a path in hand it returns -EINVAL if the inode superblock s_magic is not XFS_SB_MAGIC, then -EBADF if the inode is not a regular file, directory or symlink. Otherwise it fills a local xfs_handle: for cmd == XFS_IOC_PATH_TO_FSHANDLE only the fsid (hsize = sizeof(struct xfs_fsid), zeroed fid), for any other cmd the fsid plus the inode number and generation (hsize = sizeof(struct xfs_handle)). It then calls copy_to_user for the handle bytes to hreq->ohandle and for hsize (4 bytes) to hreq->ohandlen; if either copy fails it returns -EFAULT, in which case hreq->ohandle may already hold the handle bytes. It returns 0 only if both copies succeed. Every return after the path was obtained goes through out_put, which drops that path reference with path_put. No XFS locks are taken.
note: Read xfs_handle.c:41-140. Reviewer round-1 claim (copy_to_user failure after ohandle write) is RIGHT and in prose. Round-2 claim (unsupported inode type returns -EBADF not -EINVAL) is RIGHT: line 115-119 gives -EBADF; -EINVAL (111-113) is for non-XFS sb magic. Removed the over-broad 'before every return' on path reference.

name: xfs_file_ioctl
prose: The XFS ioctl dispatcher (xfs_ioctl.c:1177-1427): filp is the file, cmd the ioctl number, p the user-space argument cast to a __user pointer. It switches on cmd and, for most commands, simply returns the value of a per-command handler (for example xfs_ioc_trim, xfs_ioc_getlabel, xfs_ioc_fsbulkstat, xfs_ioc_getbmap, xfs_ioc_getfsmap, xfs_attrlist_by_handle, xfs_ioc_exchange_range); the result is whatever that handler returns, which can be a nonnegative number or file descriptor as well as 0 or a negative errno (for example XFS_IOC_OPEN_BY_HANDLE returns the new descriptor through xfs_open_by_handle). Commands handled inline: XFS_IOC_ALLOCSP/FREESP/ALLOCSP64/FREESP64 log a one-time warning and return -ENOTTY; XFS_IOC_DIOINFO calls vfs_getattr (returning its error), fills a dioattr and returns -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails, else 0; XFS_IOC_GETVERSION returns put_user of the inode generation; the handle commands (FD_TO_HANDLE, PATH_TO_HANDLE, PATH_TO_FSHANDLE, OPEN_BY_HANDLE, READLINK_BY_HANDLE) copy a handle request from user space (-EFAULT on failure) and return the handler result; XFS_IOC_SWAPEXT, FSGROWFSDATA, FSGROWFSLOG and FSGROWFSRT copy their argument in (-EFAULT on failure), take mnt_want_write_file (returning its error if it fails), call the operation and always call mnt_drop_write_file afterwards when it was taken; XFS_IOC_GOINGDOWN, ERROR_INJECTION and ERROR_CLEARALL return -EPERM without CAP_SYS_ADMIN and -EFAULT on a failed user copy; XFS_IOC_FREE_EOFBLOCKS returns -EPERM without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, -EROFS on a read-only mount, -EFAULT on a failed copy, the error from xfs_fs_eofblocks_from_user, else the result of xfs_blockgc_free_space bracketed by sb_start_write/sb_end_write. Any other cmd returns -ENOTTY. Locks and references used inside the delegated handlers are managed by those handlers and are not described here.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function is xfs_file_ioctl at xfs_ioctl.c:1176-1427, read in full. Reviewer claim (OPEN_BY_HANDLE returns a nonnegative fd, not 0) is RIGHT: old 'returns 0 on success' prose was too narrow; rewritten. Old prose also omitted the -ENOTTY for the ALLOCSP/FREESP family and that EPERM applies to specific commands only.

name: xfs_buffered_write_iomap_begin
prose: iomap_begin callback for buffered writes on an XFS inode (xfs_iomap.c:1752-2004): fills *iomap (and *srcmap for COW cases) for the range [offset, offset+count). Returns -EIO if the filesystem is shut down. If the inode is zoned it returns exactly the result of xfs_zoned_buffered_write_iomap_begin; if xfs_get_extsz_hint(ip) is nonzero it returns exactly the result of xfs_direct_write_iomap_begin; neither of those paths takes the inode lock here. Otherwise it calls xfs_qm_dqattach (error returned) and xfs_ilock_for_iomap (error returned, for example -EAGAIN under IOMAP_NOWAIT) which sets lockmode, then, with the inode lock held: -EFSCORRUPTED (after xfs_bmap_mark_sick) if the data fork is not in extents or btree format or if the XFS_ERRTAG_BMAPIFORMAT error tag fires; error from xfs_iread_extents; for IOMAP_UNSHARE or IOMAP_ZERO with a hole at offset it fills a hole iomap and returns 0. For IOMAP_ZERO over a delalloc extent at or beyond EOF it unlocks, calls truncate_pagecache from offset, and returns the result of xfs_bmapi_convert_delalloc on the data fork (iomap filled, srcmap NULL). For COW-capable inodes it looks in the COW fork and may return the COW extent as iomap and the data extent as srcmap; if the data extent is not shared it returns it directly; otherwise or on a hole it reserves delalloc space with xfs_bmapi_reserve_delalloc (in the COW or data fork), possibly with speculative preallocation computed by xfs_iomap_prealloc_size and rounded to the EOF alignment, and returns the resulting mapping with IOMAP_F_NEW (and IOMAP_F_SHARED for COW). Errors from xfs_bmap_trim_cow, xfs_bmapi_reserve_delalloc or xfs_bmbt_to_iomap are returned. Every return after xfs_ilock_for_iomap succeeds releases lockmode with xfs_iunlock first (the convert_delalloc path releases it before truncating the page cache), so the lock is not held on return; the function does not itself undo a delalloc reservation.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function read in full at xfs_iomap.c:1752-2004. Old prose said 'on failure no lock or delayed-allocation reservation is leaked', which is not supported by any line (no reservation undo here) and was removed; 'always released' kept but limited to paths after the lock is taken. Also fixed: hole path returns 0, and -EFSCORRUPTED applies to wrong data fork format, not to 'no extents'.

name: xfs_iomap_prealloc_size
prose: Computes a speculative preallocation size in filesystem blocks for a write at byte offset 'offset' that extends past the last extent in fork whichfork of ip, using the extent cursor icur (copied locally, not advanced for the caller; xfs_iomap.c:476-607). Returns 0 if XFS_ISIZE(ip) is less than mp->m_allocsize_blocks in bytes. Returns mp->m_allocsize_blocks if XFS_ISIZE(ip) is less than mp->m_dalign in bytes, or there is no extent before the cursor, or the previous extent ends before offset_fsb. Otherwise it sums the lengths of the contiguous preceding extents (stopping when the run exceeds XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN/2, at a delalloc extent, or at a gap), doubles that (using XFS_B_TO_FSB(offset) instead if the double exceeds XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN), caps it at roundup_pow_of_two(XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN), reduces it with free-space (data or realtime) and user, group and project quota throttle shifts, rounds a nonzero result down to a power of two and caps it at XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN, divides it by 16 repeatedly while it is nonzero and not below the free space estimate, and finally raises it to mp->m_allocsize_blocks if smaller. The final value is returned; after that last step it is not necessarily a power of two. It reads only inode, mount, quota and free-space state; it takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Read xfs_iomap.c:476-607. Reviewer round-15 claim (code returns m_allocsize_blocks for size below m_dalign, prose says returns 0 below allocsize) is WRONG as a correction but exposes the two distinct early returns: line 501-502 returns 0 for size below allocsize bytes, line 508-511 returns m_allocsize_blocks for size below m_dalign bytes (or no/early previous extent); the old prose already stated both. Old prose said 'capped at MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN ... never smaller than allocsize ... rounded to power of two' without noting the final raise can break both; qualified. Contract dropped (not purely integer, reads mount state).

name: xlog_cil_force_seq
prose: Forces the CIL push for the given commit sequence and waits for it (xfs_log_cil.c:1818-1906); sequence 0 means cil->xc_current_sequence (a debug ASSERT checks sequence <= xc_current_sequence). Loop: it calls xlog_cil_push_now(log, sequence, false), takes cil->xc_push_lock, and walks cil->xc_committing. Within the walk, for each context: if the log is shut down it goes to out_shutdown; contexts with a sequence greater than the target are skipped; a context with sequence <= target whose commit_lsn is still zero causes it to wait on xc_commit_wait (releasing xc_push_lock) and restart from xlog_cil_push_now; a context whose sequence equals the target and which has a commit_lsn records that commit_lsn. After the walk, if the target is still cil->xc_current_sequence and the CIL is not flagged empty (XLOG_CIL_EMPTY clear) it unlocks and restarts. Otherwise it unlocks and returns the recorded commit_lsn, which stays NULLCOMMITLSN if no committing context with the target sequence was found (including when the target is the current sequence and the CIL is empty, or when the target sequence is no longer on the committing list). If the shutdown check fires it unlocks and returns 0, deliberately not NULLCOMMITLSN so log-force error handling still runs. The shutdown test is only reached inside the committing-list walk, so an empty list is not checked for shutdown. xc_push_lock is not held on either return.
note: Slice cut head; real function name is xlog_cil_force_seq (xfs_log_cil.c:1818), not xlog_cil_force_lsn. Previous prose claimed NULLCOMMITLSN only when 'CIL was empty at the current sequence'; code returns it whenever no context with that sequence was found (line 1869, 1894). Shutdown only checked inside list walk (1853).

name: xlog_find_head
prose: Finds the head block of the log (xfs_log_recover.c:498-752) and stores it in *return_head_blk. It first calls xlog_find_zeroed; a negative result is warned about and returned, and a result of 1 (log is zeroed) stores the returned first_blk in *return_head_blk (warning 'totally zeroed log' if it is 0) and returns 0 without allocating a buffer. Otherwise it allocates a one-block buffer (-ENOMEM if that fails), reads block 0 and the last block with xlog_bread to get their cycle numbers, and depending on whether the cycles are equal uses the last-cycle as the stop cycle or calls xlog_find_cycle_start to locate the point where the cycle number changes. It then verifies cycle numbers with xlog_find_verify_cycle over up to XLOG_TOTAL_REC_SHIFT blocks (in one or two parts when the head is near the start), possibly moving head_blk, and validates the head with xlog_find_verify_log_record, in one or two reads, converting a positive return value 1 to -EIO. On success it frees the buffer, stores 0 in *return_head_blk if head_blk equals the log size in blocks, else head_blk, and returns 0. On any error after the buffer allocation it frees the buffer with kvfree, warns 'failed to find log head' and returns that error (from xlog_bread, xlog_find_cycle_start, xlog_find_verify_cycle or xlog_find_verify_log_record); *return_head_blk is not written on those error paths nor on the -ENOMEM and xlog_find_zeroed error returns.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function xlog_find_head at xfs_log_recover.c:498-752 read in full. Reviewer round-15 claim (zeroed-log path returns 0 without setting *return_head_blk) is WRONG: line 517 sets *return_head_blk = first_blk before return 0 at 528. Old 'buffer freed on every path' was too broad: the zeroed and ENOMEM paths return before any buffer exists; fixed.

name: xfs_mountfs
prose: Performs the main mount of an XFS filesystem from an mp whose superblock is already in mp->m_sb (xfs_mount.c:837-1288). It sets up common superblock state, may set the NLINK feature bit and mp->m_update_sb, validates the new stripe alignment and updates alignment, computes btree geometry, then initialises sysfs, scrub stats, error tags and the UUID registration (xfs_uuid_mount), checks the sparse-inode alignment, checks device sizes, calls xfs_rtmount_init, computes m_fixedfsid, and calls xfs_da_mount, xfs_initialize_perag, xfs_initialize_rtgroups, rejects a zero sb_logblocks with -EFSCORRUPTED, registers the inodegc shrinker, mounts the log (xfs_log_mount), starts inodegc and blockgc, sets up the metadir (if the feature is present), reads the root inode with xfs_iget (-EFSCORRUPTED if it is not a directory), mounts the realtime inodes, checks summary counts, may sync the superblock when not read-only, sets up quotas (xfs_qm_newmount, or resets sb_qflags), temporarily reserves per-AG blocks around xfs_log_mount_finish (an ENOSPC from that reservation is only warned about and its error code is then overwritten by the log_mount_finish result), mounts zones on zoned filesystems, mounts quotas, and, when not read-only, reserves free-space pools (failure only warns) and calls xfs_fs_reserve_ag_blocks again (any error other than -ENOSPC unwinds; -ENOSPC is tolerated, so the per-AG reservation may be missing on a successful mount), starts zone GC and finally sets the atomic-write limits (error unwinds). It returns 0 on success. On the first fatal error it jumps to a label that unwinds in reverse order: out_agresv (unreserve AG blocks, unmount quotas, unmount zones), out_rtunmount (rt inodes), out_rele_rip (release the root inode and dquots), out_free_metadir (release the metadir inode, flush inodegc and inodes, cancel the log mount), out_inodegc_shrinker, out_fail_wait (drain buftargs), then free rtgroups, perag, da state, UUID, error tags, sysfs and scrub stats; the error from the failing step is returned. Early failures (before sysfs init) jump straight to out and skip the later cleanups.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function xfs_mountfs at xfs_mount.c:837-1288 read in full. Old precondition said perag, rtgroups and log target were already set up; wrong: this function initialises perag/rtgroups/log itself (lines 996, 1003, 1032). Reviewer claim (success tolerates ENOSPC from xfs_fs_reserve_ag_blocks so reservations may be absent) is RIGHT (lines 1213-1215), added; the earlier 1152 ENOSPC is overwritten at 1156.

name: xfs_reflink_fill_delalloc
prose: Replaces a delalloc CoW-fork reservation in cmap with a real unwritten extent so the CoW fork covers the start of imap (xfs_reflink.c:516-595). Called with the inode ILOCK held via *lockmode. It loops (do/while): each pass releases the lock with xfs_iunlock(*lockmode), sets *lockmode to 0, and calls xfs_trans_alloc_inode (which retakes XFS_ILOCK_EXCL and joins the inode with no lock flags, so the lock stays held after commit or cancel). If that call fails the error is returned with the inode unlocked and *lockmode 0. Otherwise it sets *lockmode = XFS_ILOCK_EXCL, re-reads imap with xfs_bmapi_read if the data fork i_df.if_seq changed while unlocked, and calls xfs_find_trim_cow_extent. If that fails or reports not shared, it cancels the transaction and returns that error (0 when merely not shared). If a real CoW extent was found it cancels the transaction and exits the loop. Otherwise it allocates the delalloc range with xfs_bmapi_write (COW fork, preallocate; error cancels the transaction and is returned), sets the cowblocks tag, and commits (a commit error is returned; the transaction is consumed). The loop repeats while the resulting cmap extent ends at or before imap->br_startoff. After leaving the loop it returns the result of xfs_reflink_convert_unwritten (which trims cmap to imap and, if convert_now is set and the extent is unwritten, converts it, returning any error). On every return after xfs_trans_alloc_inode succeeded the inode ILOCK is still held with *lockmode == XFS_ILOCK_EXCL and no transaction is outstanding.
note: Read xfs_reflink.c:516-595 and xfs_trans_alloc_inode (xfs_trans.c:1062-1110). Reviewer claims (trans_alloc_inode failure has no transaction to cancel; commit error path does not cancel because commit consumes it) are RIGHT and match old prose. Old prose omitted the do/while loop (lines 530-588) and the retry condition; added.

name: xfs_reflink_end_cow_extent
prose: Remaps at most one written CoW-fork extent of ip in the file block range starting at *offset_fsb and ending before end_fsb into the data fork (xfs_reflink.c:938-963). The caller must not hold XFS_ILOCK_EXCL on ip. It allocates a transaction with xfs_trans_alloc (write reservation, XFS_TRANS_RESERVE); if that fails the error is returned with no lock taken and *offset_fsb unchanged. Otherwise it takes XFS_ILOCK_EXCL, joins the inode with no lock flags, and calls xfs_reflink_end_cow_extent_locked. That helper returns 0 and sets *offset_fsb = end_fsb when there is no written CoW extent in the range; returns an error from xfs_iext_count_extend, xfs_bmapi_read or xfs_bunmapi with *offset_fsb unchanged; and on success remaps the extent (data-fork unmap, refcount decrease, quota update, map into the data fork, remove from the CoW fork) and sets *offset_fsb to the end of the remapped piece. If the helper returned an error the transaction is cancelled and that error is returned; otherwise xfs_trans_commit is called and its result is returned, so a commit error is returned with *offset_fsb possibly already advanced. After the lock is taken, XFS_ILOCK_EXCL is released on every return.
note: Read xfs_reflink.c:825-963. Reviewer claims (no-op success sets *offset_fsb = end_fsb; commit failure omitted; alloc failure does not take the lock) are RIGHT and are covered. No reviewer claim was wrong.

name: xfs_init_procfs
prose: Creates the procfs entries for XFS (xfs_stats.c:142-163, only compiled with CONFIG_PROC_FS). It calls proc_mkdir("fs/xfs") and returns -ENOMEM at once if that fails, having created nothing. Then it calls proc_symlink("fs/xfs/stat") pointing at /sys/fs/xfs/stats/stats, and, only when CONFIG_XFS_QUOTA is set, proc_create_single for "fs/xfs/xqmstat" and "fs/xfs/xqm". If any of those later calls fails it calls remove_proc_subtree("fs/xfs", NULL), which removes the directory and everything under it, and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise it returns 0. It takes no arguments and does not check whether the entries already exist.
note: Read xfs_stats.c:142-163. Old contract dropped: the function mutates global procfs state and mechanical review kept rejecting the contract; prose is unchanged in substance.

name: xfs_trans_read_buf_map
prose: Reads (or finds) the metadata buffer described by target/map/nmaps and returns it locked in *bpp (xfs_trans_buf.c:226-332). It sets *bpp = NULL first, so *bpp stays NULL on every failure. If tp is non-NULL and the buffer is already attached to tp (xfs_trans_buf_item_match): if the filesystem is shut down it returns -EIO without releasing the buffer; otherwise it calls xfs_buf_reverify, and if that fails it logs, forces a SHUTDOWN_META_IO_ERROR shutdown when tp has XFS_TRANS_DIRTY, converts -EFSBADCRC to -EFSCORRUPTED and returns the error without releasing the buffer; on success it increments bli_recur, sets *bpp and returns 0 (the caller releases with xfs_trans_brelse, which decrements bli_recur). If the buffer is not attached it calls xfs_buf_read_map: on error 0 continues; -ENOMEM and -EAGAIN are returned as they are; any other error first forces the shutdown if tp is non-NULL and dirty, then is returned. After a successful read, if the filesystem is shut down it releases the buffer with xfs_buf_relse and returns -EIO; otherwise it joins the buffer to tp with _xfs_trans_bjoin when tp is non-NULL, sets *bpp and returns 0 (the caller releases with xfs_trans_brelse, or xfs_buf_relse when tp is NULL).
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function xfs_trans_read_buf_map at xfs_trans_buf.c:226-332 read in full. Note my earlier line filter hid '*bpp' lines; re-read raw lines 236-330. Prose agrees with the previous wording on all return paths; added that *bpp is NULL on failure (line 240) and the shutdown conditions.

name: do_header
prose: Parses a newc cpio header held in collected (initramfs.c:279-310). If the first six bytes are "070701" it sets csum_present to false, if "070702" to true; otherwise it calls error() with "incorrect cpio method used: use -H newc option" when the six bytes are "070707", or with "no cpio magic" for anything else, and returns 1. For a valid magic it calls parse_header(collected), sets next_header = (this_header + N_ALIGN(name_len) + body_len + 3) & ~3, sets state to SkipIt, and then returns 0 in every remaining case: immediately (state stays SkipIt) if name_len <= 0 or name_len > PATH_MAX; for a symlink (S_ISLNK(mode)) with body_len > PATH_MAX (state stays SkipIt); for a symlink with body_len <= PATH_MAX it sets collect = collected = symlink_buf, remains = N_ALIGN(name_len) + body_len, next_state = GotSymlink and state = Collect; for any other entry that is a regular file or has body_len == 0 it calls read_into(name_buf, N_ALIGN(name_len), GotName), which either points collected at the already-buffered data and sets state to GotName, or starts a Collect into name_buf; for every other entry (non-regular, non-symlink, with a nonzero body_len) nothing more is scheduled and state remains SkipIt.
note: Read initramfs.c:243-310. Reviewer round-2 claim (symlink with body_len > PATH_MAX schedules a name read; code leaves state SkipIt) is RIGHT; old prose said 'no read scheduled in remaining cases' but missed the name_len bounds early return (296-297); rewritten. Round-1 precondition claim not applied: contract left empty.

name: do_name
prose: Handles a cpio entry name held in collected (initramfs.c:361-412). It first sets state to SkipIt and next_state to Reset. If collected[name_len - 1] is not a NUL byte it calls pr_err and error("malformed archive") and returns 1. Otherwise it returns 0 after one of: for the name "TRAILER!!!", free_hash(); otherwise clean_path(collected, mode) (removes an existing entry of a different file type) and then, by type: for a regular file, maybe_link() is called; if it returns -1 nothing more happens and state stays SkipIt; otherwise filp_open(collected, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_LARGEFILE, mode) is used with O_TRUNC added only when maybe_link() did not return 1; if the open fails state stays SkipIt, else wfile_pos and io_csum are set to 0, vfs_fchown and vfs_fchmod are called, vfs_truncate to body_len when body_len is non-zero, and state is set to CopyFile; for a directory, init_mkdir, init_chown, init_chmod and dir_add are called (their errors are ignored); for a block or character device, fifo or socket, maybe_link() is called and only when it returns 0 are init_mknod, init_chown, init_chmod and do_utime called (a hard link may exist when it returned 1, and nothing is created when it returned -1); other file types do nothing further. Return values from the chown, chmod, mknod, mkdir and truncate helpers are not checked. A hard link may already have been created by maybe_link() before a regular-file open failure.
note: Read initramfs.c:333-412 (clean_path, maybe_link, do_name). Reviewer claims from rounds 1-2 (open/maybe_link failure returns 0 with no new open file; maybe_link may already have hard-linked) are RIGHT and in the prose. No claim was wrong.

name: do_mq_notify
prose: Implements mq_notify for descriptor mqdes with a kernel-space struct sigevent notification that may be NULL (mqueue.c:1291-1398). It first calls audit_mq_notify. If notification is non-NULL: -EINVAL if sigev_notify is not SIGEV_NONE, SIGEV_SIGNAL or SIGEV_THREAD, or if it is SIGEV_SIGNAL with an invalid sigev_signo. For SIGEV_THREAD it allocates a NOTIFY_COOKIE_LEN skb (-ENOMEM on failure), copies the cookie from sigev_value.sival_ptr (kfree_skb and -EFAULT on failure), looks up the netlink socket whose fd is sigev_signo with netlink_getsockbyfd (kfree_skb and its error on failure), and calls netlink_attachskb, retrying the socket lookup while it returns 1; for any other nonzero result it returns that result immediately (netlink_attachskb itself frees the skb and drops the socket reference on a negative return, per its comment). Then it looks up the descriptor: -EBADF if it is not an open file or its f_op is not mqueue_file_operations; goto out in these cases releases the netlink socket and skb with netlink_detachskb if sock is still held. Under info->lock: with a NULL notification, if the current thread group owns the notification it is removed (remove_notification) and the inode atime/ctime updated, and otherwise nothing changes and 0 is returned; with a non-NULL notification and an existing owner it returns -EBUSY; otherwise it records the SIGEV_NONE, SIGEV_THREAD (taking over sock and nc, which are then cleared) or SIGEV_SIGNAL settings, stores notify_owner = get_pid(task_tgid(current)) and notify_user_ns = get_user_ns(current_user_ns()), and updates atime/ctime. The success and -EBUSY paths fall to out, which detaches sock and nc only if they were not taken over. Returns 0 on success.
note: Read mqueue.c:1291-1398 and netlink_attachskb/netlink_detachskb (af_netlink.c:1203-1256, 1277-1281). Reviewer round-15 claim (attachskb failure returns without freeing nc) is WRONG: netlink_attachskb frees the skb and drops the socket reference on error (af_netlink.c:1207, 1233, 1251). Round-1 (NULL deregistration by non-owner returns 0 unchanged; sival_ptr must be readable) and round-2 (invalid sigev_notify returns -EINVAL) claims are RIGHT and incorporated; precondition no longer requires valid fields.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(mq_open, const char __user *, u_name,
prose: Generated compat system call for mq_open(u_name, oflag, mode, u_attr) defined at mqueue.c:1518-1529. If u_attr is non-NULL and O_CREAT is set in oflag, it calls get_compat_mq_attr into a local struct mq_attr and returns -EFAULT if that fails; otherwise (including when u_attr is non-NULL but O_CREAT is clear) it passes a NULL attribute pointer. It then returns the result of do_mq_open(u_name, oflag, mode, p), which is a file descriptor or a negative errno. This function itself takes no locks and holds no reference.

name: ksys_semctl
prose: Dispatches a semctl operation (sem.c:1651-1703); semid, semnum, cmd, arg and version come from the caller (arg is an unsigned long that is treated as a user pointer p). It returns -EINVAL if semid < 0, then switches on cmd. IPC_INFO and SEM_INFO return semctl_info's result. IPC_STAT, SEM_STAT and SEM_STAT_ANY call semctl_stat into a local semid64_ds; a negative result is returned, otherwise the data is copied to p with copy_semid_to_user and, if that copy returns non-zero (a failed copy or an unknown version), the result is -EFAULT, else the non-negative value returned by semctl_stat (0 for IPC_STAT, the segment index for SEM_STAT and SEM_STAT_ANY). GETALL, GETVAL, GETPID, GETNCNT, GETZCNT and SETALL return semctl_main's result. SETVAL returns semctl_setval with val taken as the low 32 bits of arg (the high half on 64-bit big-endian). IPC_SET copies the semid64 data from p with copy_semid_from_user and returns -EFAULT if that returns non-zero (a bad buffer or an unknown version); then, like IPC_RMID, it returns semctl_down's result. Any other cmd returns -EINVAL. The results of the delegated helpers can be non-negative values (value, pid, count, index) or negative errnos. ksys_semctl itself takes no locks; locking is done inside the semctl_* helpers.
note: Read sem.c:1651-1703. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: unknown version in IPC_SET returns -EFAULT (1695-1696); SEM_STAT returns semctl_stat's non-negative result not 0 (1670-1675); positive values come from GET*/INFO. The old prose's claim that every lock is released inside helpers was dropped as not shown in this function. Slice also contained compat_ksys_semctl (1774-1817), which is a separate function not listed.

prose: Generated system call entry for semctl(semid, semnum, cmd, arg) defined at sem.c:1705-1708. It returns ksys_semctl(semid, semnum, cmd, arg, IPC_64) unchanged: whatever that function returns (a non-negative value such as a semaphore value, pid, wait count, segment index or 0, or a negative errno). It takes no locks and holds no reference itself.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(semtimedop, int, semid, struct sembuf __user *, tsops,
prose: Generated system call entry for semtimedop(semid, tsops, nsops, timeout) defined at sem.c:2268-2272. It returns ksys_semtimedop(semid, tsops, nsops, timeout). That function, if timeout is non-NULL, copies it with get_timespec64 and returns -EFAULT if the copy fails, and then returns do_semtimedop(semid, tsops, nsops, &ts) (or with NULL if timeout is NULL). do_semtimedop returns -E2BIG if nsops > the namespace sc_semopm, -EINVAL if nsops < 1, -ENOMEM if the kvmalloc_array for more than SEMOPM_FAST entries fails, -EFAULT if copy_from_user of the sembuf array fails (freeing any allocation), and otherwise the result of __do_semtimedop. User pointers are not required to be readable; bad ones give -EFAULT.

It returns compat_ksys_semtimedop(semid, tsems, nsops, timeout), which, if timeout is non-NULL, copies it with get_old_timespec32 and returns -EFAULT if that fails, and then returns do_semtimedop(semid, tsems, nsops, &ts) (or NULL when timeout is NULL). do_semtimedop returns -E2BIG if nsops exceeds the namespace sc_semopm, -EINVAL if nsops < 1, -ENOMEM if a large sembuf array cannot be allocated, -EFAULT if the array cannot be copied from user space, and otherwise the result of __do_semtimedop.

prose: Generated system call entry for semop(semid, tsops, nsops) defined at sem.c:2296-2300. It returns do_semtimedop(semid, tsops, nsops, NULL): -E2BIG if nsops exceeds the namespace sc_semopm, -EINVAL if nsops < 1, -ENOMEM if a large sembuf array cannot be allocated, -EFAULT if copying the array from user space fails (any allocation is freed), and otherwise the value returned by __do_semtimedop.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(shmdt, char __user *, shmaddr)
prose: Generated system call entry for shmdt(shmaddr) defined at shm.c:1836-1839; it returns ksys_shmdt(shmaddr). ksys_shmdt returns -EINVAL if the address is not page aligned; otherwise it takes mmap_write_lock_killable on current->mm, returning -EINTR if that fails. On an MMU build it scans the VMAs from the address; the first VMA with shm_vm_ops whose (vm_start - addr)/PAGE_SIZE equals vm_pgoff is unmapped with do_vmi_align_munmap (its result is ignored), retval becomes 0, and later VMAs of the same file within the segment size with the same property are unmapped too; if no VMA matches, retval stays -EINVAL. On a non-MMU build it unmaps the VMA that starts exactly at addr if it uses shm_vm_ops and returns 0, else -EINVAL. The mmap lock is released before returning. Detaching (the attach count decrement) happens through the VMA close operation when the VMA is removed, not in this function.
note: Read shm.c:1735-1839. Reviewer claim (omits -EINTR from mmap_write_lock_killable) is RIGHT (line 1745-1746); do_munmap error is ignored (1788-1789, 1813-1814, and 1826 non-MMU), so a failed unmap would still return 0 -- stated. Slice only held the tail of ksys_shmdt.

name: audit_log_start
prose: Starts a new audit record and returns a buffer or NULL (audit.c:1908-1976). It returns NULL if audit_initialized is not AUDIT_INITIALIZED, or if audit_filter(type, AUDIT_FILTER_EXCLUDE) rejects the type. If the current task is neither the auditd task nor the audit control owner, it loops while audit_backlog_limit is non-zero and the audit queue is longer than that limit: each pass wakes kauditd, and if gfp_mask allows blocking and the remaining wait time is above 0 it sleeps uninterruptibly (accumulating actual wait time); otherwise it emits a rate-limited warning, calls audit_log_lost("backlog limit exceeded") and returns NULL. The auditd task and audit control owner skip this loop entirely. Then it calls audit_buffer_alloc (kmem_cache_alloc, nlmsg_new and nlmsg_put); on failure it calls audit_log_lost("out of memory in audit_log_start") and returns NULL. Otherwise it stamps the buffer with audit_get_stamp(ab->ctx): from the context via auditsc_get_stamp if ctx is non-NULL and that call succeeds, else the coarse current time and a new audit_serial(); it clears ctx->dummy when ctx is non-NULL; writes the header "audit(<sec>.<msec>:<serial>): " with audit_log_format and returns the buffer. The caller owns the returned buffer and must finish or free it (audit_log_end / audit_buffer_free). It may sleep when gfp_mask allows blocking.
note: Read audit.c:1818-1976. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: (1) NULL when backlog stays exceeded after the wait time is used up (1949-1955); (2) auditd / ctl-owner bypass (1928); (3) stamp falls back to fresh time/serial if auditsc_get_stamp fails (1887-1890). Prose now states all three.

name: audit_set_enabled
prose: Changes audit_enabled to state (audit.c:482-493). If state > AUDIT_LOCKED it returns -EINVAL and changes nothing. Otherwise it calls audit_do_config_change("audit_enabled", &audit_enabled, state), whose result is returned, and, only when that result is 0, sets audit_ever_enabled |= !!state. audit_do_config_change behaves by the current audit_enabled value: if AUDIT_OFF, the new value is stored and 0 returned without logging; if AUDIT_ENABLE, it logs an AUDIT_CONFIG_CHANGE record through audit_log_config_change: if audit_log_start returns NULL (no buffer) the helper returns 0 and the value is stored and 0 returned; if the record is logged but audit_log_task_context returns a nonzero error, the value is not stored and that error is returned; otherwise the value is stored and 0 returned. If AUDIT_LOCKED, the value is never stored: it returns the nonzero audit_log_task_context error if the record was logged and that call failed, and otherwise -EPERM (including when no log buffer could be started).
note: Read audit.c:421-493. Reviewer claims: round 2 (logging error code is returned, not -EPERM) RIGHT; round 15 (when audit_log_start fails rc stays 0, so the change is applied and 0 returned for AUDIT_ENABLE) RIGHT (audit.c:427-429, 458-459); round 1 (not all nonzero results are -EPERM) RIGHT. Prose rewritten to state exactly this; no claim was wrong.

name: audit_set_failure
prose: Changes audit_failure to state (audit.c:495-503). If state is not AUDIT_FAIL_SILENT, AUDIT_FAIL_PRINTK or AUDIT_FAIL_PANIC it returns -EINVAL and changes nothing. Otherwise it returns audit_do_config_change("audit_failure", &audit_failure, state): if audit_enabled is AUDIT_OFF the value is stored and 0 returned without logging; if AUDIT_ENABLE it logs an AUDIT_CONFIG_CHANGE record, and the value is stored and 0 returned unless audit_log_task_context fails, in which case the value is not stored and that nonzero error is returned (if no audit buffer could be started the logging step returns 0, so the value is stored); if AUDIT_LOCKED the value is never stored and the result is the nonzero audit_log_task_context error if logging failed that way, otherwise -EPERM.
note: Read audit.c:421-503. Reviewer claims (logging error code returned instead of -EPERM; audit_log_start failure leaves rc 0 so the change is applied) are RIGHT and are now stated; none wrong.

name: kauditd_thread
prose: Body of the kauditd kernel thread (audit.c:879-954); the argument is unused. It calls set_freezable() and then loops while kthread_should_stop() is false. Each iteration: under rcu_read_lock it reads auditd_conn; if NULL it unlocks and jumps straight to the main-queue step with sk = NULL, without touching the hold or retry queues and without calling auditd_reset. If non-NULL it takes a reference on ac->net with get_net, gets the netlink socket and portid, then calls kauditd_send_queue on audit_hold_queue (retries 5, failed skbs re-held) and, only if that returns >= 0, on audit_retry_queue (failed skbs held); if either returns < 0 it sets sk = NULL, calls auditd_reset(ac) and skips to the main-queue step. Main-queue step: kauditd_send_queue on audit_queue with one retry and the multicast callback; failed skbs go to the retry queue if sk is non-NULL, else to the hold queue; then if ac is non-NULL and that send returned < 0 it calls auditd_reset(ac). It then sets sk = NULL, drops the net reference if one was taken, calls wake_up(&audit_backlog_wait) and calls wait_event_freezable(kauditd_wait, audit_queue is non-empty). That wait does not test kthread_should_stop; it returns when the audit queue is non-empty or the wait is interrupted by a signal, so a stop request takes effect only after the wait returns and the loop condition is re-evaluated. The function returns 0 only after the loop exits.
note: Read audit.c:879-954. Reviewer claims: round 1 (hold/retry queues not always drained) RIGHT; round 2 (no-auditd path skips to main_queue without auditd_reset) RIGHT (894-897); round 15 (wait_event_freezable condition does not include kthread_should_stop, so stop/freeze do not end the wait) RIGHT (949-950). Old prose claim 'sleeps until queue non-empty or the thread is stopped or frozen' removed.

name: audit_filter
prose: Evaluates the audit filter rules of list audit_filter_list[listtype] against the current task for message type msgtype (auditfilter.c:1339-1409). Under rcu_read_lock it walks the rules in order; for each rule it checks every field in turn: AUDIT_PID (task tgid), AUDIT_UID, AUDIT_GID, AUDIT_LOGINUID, AUDIT_LOGINUID_SET, AUDIT_MSGTYPE, the LSM subject fields (compared with security_audit_rule_match only when the field has an lsm_rule, otherwise the field counts as not matching) and AUDIT_EXE (compare then optional negation). If a field's result is 0 the rule is abandoned and the next rule is tried; if a field has any other type, or a comparison returns a negative result, the scan stops at once and the function returns 1. A rule with zero fields never matches. For the first rule whose fields all match, the function returns 0 if the rule action is AUDIT_NEVER or listtype is AUDIT_FILTER_EXCLUDE, and stops scanning; with any other action (for example AUDIT_POSSIBLE or AUDIT_ALWAYS) on a non-exclude list it returns 1. It returns 1 as well when no rule fully matches. The RCU read lock is released on every return; listtype is used as an array index without a range check.
note: Read auditfilter.c:1339-1409. Reviewer round-2 claim (AUDIT_POSSIBLE also returns 1) RIGHT and covered by the 'any other action' wording. Contract dropped (reads global lists, current task; and the earlier contract was rejected by Frama-C). 'Exactly when some rule ...' in the old prose was imprecise: only the first fully matching rule matters and an earlier error/unsupported field stops the scan.
